thread:
incident-bot: P1 — DNS resolver anomalies detected in eu-west. Pager triggered by 503 spikes and origin mismatch. Auto-runbook kicked off.
ashley: I'm looking — Grafana shows sudden spike in 5xx from customers with eu-west resolver IPs. Curious: they are getting IPs for us-east backends.
mira: Confirming — traced a couple requests from EU customers, their A records resolve to 54.23.12.34 (us-east) instead of 18.194.22.11 (eu-west) for service.rw-inference.com
ashley: Paste dig from one of my laptop queries:
```
$ dig +short service.rw-inference.com @8.8.8.8
54.23.12.34
```
ashley: TTL is 300 but we've rolled a eu-west change earlier today. Looks like some resolvers still serving cached/eP-routed answers.
devon: Can we force a change? Route53 geolocation policy still shows eu-west weight 100, us-east 0. Health checks show eu-west healthy.
cloudops: I see Cloudflare in front for some customers — CF's resolver cache may be sticky, plus we've got a custom weighted GeoDNS in front of Route53 in some regions.
mira: I'm seeing NXDOMAIN from a subset of DoT resolvers — probably propagation inconsistency between authoritative servers.
ashley: Quick mitigation options:
- Short term: create a low-TTL failover DNS entry with explicit eu-west A record and update Cloudflare zone override (if applicable)
- Mid term: update Route53 health checks and force weight flip to route traffic
- Longer term: do a manual flush via CF API and open support with AWS/CF
zara-cs: CS reporting ~12 customers seeing errors, mostly in DE/NL. Some apps auto-retry and succeed in 10-30s.
devon: I'll take the API path — pushing a temporary 60s TTL and add explicit eu-west A record on CF edge via API. This should reduce cross-region routing within ~TTL window.
ashley: Do it and post API call. Also add a cloudflare purge for service.rw-inference.com record.
devon: Running CF override now:
```
curl -X PATCH 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/ZONEID/dns_records/RECORDID' \ 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**' \ 
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
 --data '{"content":"18.194.22.11","ttl":60}'
```
devon: Response 200. TTL updated to 60 and content set to eu-west IP. Also triggered zone cache purge.
mira: Ran dig from multiple public resolvers — some still unpropagated but majority now show eu-west.
nashley: Opened two support tickets: AWS SR# 1234567890 (Route53 inconsistent SOA propagation), CF ticket #987654 for edge cache remain. Link: https://support.cloudflare.com/tickets/987654
cloudops: Spun up 2 proxy instances in eu-central as fallback to terminate traffic that mistakenly lands in us-east. Nginx config applied to proxy to backhaul to eu-west.
nashley: That's live. Updating incident status to mitigated->partial. Customer impact reduced to ~1-2 customers with intermittent failures.
zara-cs: Noted. CS will message affected customers with temporary workaround: disable aggressive resolver caching or restart app DNS cache.
incident-bot: Note: On-call handoff scheduled. ashley handing to devon for night shift at 23:00 UTC.
ashley: Handoff notes:
- Mitigation done: CF record override and TTL lowered to 60
- AWS SR opened, CF ticket opened
- Proxy fallback in eu-central is live; routing rules on edge adjusted
- Monitor: request5xx rate, DNS A record variance, Cloudflare cache hit/miss
- Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/infrastructure/dns-incident-runbook
devon: Acked. I'll monitor through the night, ping if anything reappears.
mira: Added a datapoint: traceroute from NL to us-east host shows asymmetric path — possible anycast/resolver misrouting causing client to query wrong authoritative server. Adding to AWS ticket.
nashley: We'll do postmortem tomorrow. Owner: ashley + cloudops. Tentative Sev1-> Sev2 at 02:00 UTC if stable.
zara-cs: Customers patched and on-call notified. Closing CS loop for initial outreach.
devon: Will document exact sequence of CF API calls and Route53 weight changes in the incident notes.
nashley: Thanks everyone. Adding timeline to the incident channel shortly. :white_check_mark:
